- Dependency plan: D06 gives coal(2024) - coal(2019) = -182 TWh (window dated by the same paragraph's gas sentence and "from 17% in 2019 to 29% in 2024"); D07 gives coal(2025) - coal(2021) = -162 TWh and coal(2025) - coal(2024) = -14 TWh; hence coal(2024) - coal(2021) = -148 and coal(2021) - coal(2019) = -182 + 148 = -34 TWh. Implied levels (from D06's -40%): 2019 about 455, 2024 about 273, 2021 about 421 TWh.
- Universe: not applicable (single numeric answer).
- Necessity: D06 (Doc 3) is the only source that anchors 2019 in TWh; D07 (Doc 4) is the only source that anchors 2021 in TWh. Searches for EU/European Union + coal, "2019", "2021", "since 2021", "last five years" across all eight documents: D04 L63 prints only the 2020 EU fall as a percentage ("EU (-20%)"), D05 L229 only the sign of 2021 against 2019 ("remained below 2019 levels"), D02 L345 a first-half 2023 change, D03 L353 a first-half 2025 change, D06 L1068 the 2024 change only, D07 L1020 the 2025 change and shares (9.2%, 16% in 2022). Without D06, nothing fixes 2019 (the D04 percentage needs a level); without D07, nothing fixes 2021. Removal probes pending.
- Selected-lever checks: scatter the pieces and calculate across documents, with answer-shaped printed decoys on the path: -182 (2019-2024), -162 (2021-2025), -148 (2021-2024, derived) and -20 (windows set against each other without removing 2025). A wrong sign on the 2025 step gives -6. Rebuilding levels from the rounded percentages (-40%, -5%) is unstable: the "-5%" alone, read between 4.5% and 5.5%, moves the 2019-2021 change from +4 to -53 TWh, so only the printed TWh changes give a precise answer.
- Calculation verification: caller python (-182 - (-162 - (-14)) = -34); fresh blind solver (sketch screen, runs/sketch-r1/returns.md) independently got -34 TWh by the same window algebra and checked the sign against D05 L229.
- Semantic/ID/overview probes: no document prints an EU coal figure for 2019, 2020 or 2021 in TWh, or any 2019-2021 change; the capture overview (Doc 3, Doc 4 entries) lists no EU coal figure.
- Precision/readings: inputs are whole TWh, so the exact value lies about -32.5 to -35.5; every route using the printed TWh figures gives -34. The reading of "last five years" as 2020-2024 is contradicted by the same paragraph's 2019 dates (and would leave 2019-2021 unanswerable). The sketch closed-book solve answered about -27 (low confidence, estimate band -25 to -30), so a percentage ask would be guessable; TWh precision is kept.
- Completeness: capture complete (8 of 8, no gap markers); charts are "Loading data..." placeholders in the originals too, absent for every reader alike; no EU coal chart values are needed.
- Style/set review: first question on this bundle; plain wording, 23 words. Token overlap with all workspace questions: highest ratio 0.37 (aq-00998 q01), longest shared run 4 tokens.

The D07 L1036 sentence contains a curly apostrophe ("EU’s"), so its quote is split into two straight-text spans on either side of it.
sections.question: How much did coal-fired electricity generation in the European Union change from 2019 to 2021? Give the answer in TWh with its sign.
sections.reasoning:
Step 1 (Doc 3): In its European Union section, the review of 2024 says "Over the last five years, coal generation has fallen by 182 TWh (-40%)". The same paragraph dates that window: gas "was 139 TWh (-24%) lower in 2024 than it was in 2019". So EU coal generation fell 182 TWh from 2019 to 2024.

Step 2 (Doc 4): In its European Union section, the review of 2025 says EU fossil generation "declined by 24% (-257 TWh) between 2021 and 2025", and that coal generation accounted for "(-162 TWh) since 2021" of that decline. So EU coal generation fell 162 TWh from 2021 to 2025.

Step 3 (Doc 4): EU coal generation "declined by 5% (-14 TWh) in 2025". Removing 2025 from the 2021 window gives the change from 2021 to 2024: -162 + 14 = -148 TWh.

Step 4 (Doc 3 and Doc 4): The 2019 window and the 2021 window now both end in 2024, so the change from 2019 to 2021 is -182 + 148 = -34 TWh.

Step 5 (Doc 3 and Doc 4): Setting the two printed windows against each other without removing 2025 gives -182 + 162 = -20 TWh. That is wrong, because the 2021 window ends in 2025 while the 2019 window ends in 2024.
